transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Time: 09:00 PT (16:00Z)
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Ruiz (Redwood CSM); James Carter (Auriga CTO), Elena Morales (Head of AI), Ravi Singh (DevOps), Priya Nair (Product)

Summary (auto): quick QBR to review usage, cost drivers, reliability, and next steps for potential Dedicated trial.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time for the QBR. we have a short agenda — usage, cost, reliability, roadmap, and next steps. laura and i will jump in on the technical bits. maya's here for adoption. how's everyone doing?

[00:12] James: good, thanks. busy week but excited to see the numbers.

[00:20] Elena: yeah hi, thanks. we mainly want to understand the cost spikes we saw in late april and the options for more predictable latency during business hours.

[00:30] Laura: got it. we'll walk through the usage graphs and the KV cache notes — i wanna flag that a lot of the tail latency looked like it was due to small bursts with cold kv cache misses and some request patterns that prevent batching.

[00:45] Ravi: just to call out, we had a spike on 4/28 when a marketing campaign drove chat volume, and our autoscaling didn't keep up for the first 3 minutes. that caused errors in the customer-facing flow.

[01:00] Samir: ok, thanks. we'll show the trace for that incident. quick housekeeping: i will, uh, share the dedicated pricing doc after the call and laura will attach the benchmark sheet.

[01:20] Maya: also i wanted to confirm your adoption goals this quarter — the success metrics you shared in the last sync were 99th p99 latency under 600ms for chat, and embeddings at under 200ms for API calls. are those still accurate?

[01:32] Elena: yes, p99 under 600ms is the target. cost per 1k tokens is another internal KPI. we're watching it closely.

[01:40] Laura: quick note: depending on model choice and quantization, you can see a 20-40% cost swing. also batching and cache-hit-rate influence per-token cost a lot.

[01:55] James: can you clarify the difference between hosted and dedicated here? what do we get for latency guarantees vs cost?

[02:05] Samir: yes — hosted gives immediate scale, pay-as-you-go, typical median latencies under 200ms for small chat models, but variance increases under very spiky traffic. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit, and we can tune for lower tail latency. Dedicated also gives you stronger isolation and can live in your VPC for private deployments.

[02:28] Ravi: will Dedicated require a lot of integration work? our infra team is stretched.

[02:35] Laura: minimal integration — control plane stays with Redwood by default, but we offer Private options if you need on-prem or customer-controlled control plane. For Dedicated we provide an autoscaling policy you can set, and our SEs will help size the pool. there's a short onboarding with checking network, SSO, and KMS configs.

[02:55] Priya: on the security side, auditors asked about KMS and key rotation. do you support external KMS/HSM?

[03:03] Samir: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration and HSM options in Private deployments; we'll share the security pack with SOC2, ISO notes, and the KMS flow.

[03:15] Elena: is audit log retention configurable? auditors asked for six months of immutable logs.

[03:23] Maya: yep, audit logs retention tiers can be extended as an add-on — we'll detail retention costs in the security pack.

[03:34] Laura: back to the reliability incident — i pulled the traces. the 4/28 spike shows a burst from a single campaign hitting a chat route. autoscaler had a lag; because the KV cache was cold, the per-request latency spiked and batching couldn't collapse requests. there were also retries from the client that amplified load.

[03:58] Elena: any quick mitigation we should do right away?

[04:05] Laura: short term: increase min replicas for that route during campaign windows, enable prefix-KV warming for predictable flows, and tune client retry/backoff to avoid thundering-herd. long term: dedicated capacity with warm pools will give the best p99.

[04:25] Samir: i'll note those as action items. laura, can you send the exact CLI snippets we recommend?

[04:31] Laura: yes, i'll put them in the benchmark sheet.

[04:40] James: curious about model variants — we're currently on a custom fine-tuned model, but for cost reasons we experimented with a smaller quantized variant. quality dropped on a few intents. how do you recommend managing rollouts?

[04:55] Laura: we recommend canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. Redwood Console supports per-route model pinning and A/B. For quantization, we have verified profiles — sometimes 4-bit quant works well but not for all tasks, so you want eval prompts tied to quality monitoring.

[05:15] Elena: that monitoring piece is critical — we need regression alerts tied to our eval set.

[05:20] Maya: we can set up a quality regression alert that watches chosen prompts and notifies you on drift or metric degradation.

[05:28] Ravi: on networking, our security team wants VPC peering for Dedicated. is that supported?

[05:34] Samir: yes, Dedicated can be deployed in a VPC with customer-controlled networking. for Private/on-prem we support air-gapped deployments as well, but that requires a different SOW.

[05:46] James: what's the SLA for Dedicated?

[05:50] Samir: Dedicated comes with an SLA backed uptime and latency targets — we can share the SLA doc. for hosted, we have a standard uptime commitment but not the same latency SLO guarantee as reserved pools.

[06:05] Elena: cost — can you show the rough delta between pay-as-you-go hosted and committed Dedicated for our current usage profile?

[06:13] Samir: yes, we ran a run-rate calc based on your last 30 days — at your current average token volumes and peak patterns, a moderate 6-month commit could reduce unit costs by ~28% compared to hosted list, with dedicated reducing p99 by ~150-300ms during peak bursts. i'll include the worksheet.

[06:35] Priya: is there minimum commitment? we want to avoid long lock-ins.

[06:40] Samir: minimal commitment tiers start at three months for pilot reserved pools; enterprise contracts have flexible terms. we'll lay that out.

[06:50] Laura: another operational note: our routing can do smart fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, requests can overflow to hosted compatible model variants automatically so your service stays online. that helps avoid outage during unexpected peaks.

[07:06] Ravi: that's useful. the overflow needs to keep data isolation guarantees — how is that handled?

[07:12] Samir: overflow can be configured to route to a Redwood-hosted model in a non-customer-shared environment or to another reserved pool; we can control data retention policies per route. we'll include details in the security notes.

[07:26] James: can you walk us through a sample timeline if we decide to pilot Dedicated?

[07:32] Samir: sure — week 0: sizing workshop with SE and DevOps; week 1-2: provisioning and network setup, KMS and SSO integration; week 2-4: load testing and warmup, run perf benchmarks; week 4: pilot go-live, monitor and adjust. total pilot ~4-6 weeks depending on infra approvals.

[07:52] Elena: what do you need from us for the sizing workshop?

[07:56] Laura: last 30-90 days of traffic, peak QPS windows, average seq lengths for chat, and our list of critical routes. ravi, that last 30 days export you mentioned — that will be perfect.

[08:09] Ravi: i'll get that by next week.

[08:12] Maya: a few adoption suggestions: consider converting lower-priority non-customer-facing flows to a cheaper quantized model to save costs while keeping the main userflow on full quality. also tag routes by cost center so billing is clearer.

[08:27] Priya: that tagging idea helps product finance.

[08:30] Samir: ok, quick check on compliance items — we'll attach SOC2 report, encryption notes, and KMS architecture. i'll also include an example security diagram for Dedicated in a VPC.

[08:43] Elena: thanks — auditors will want that.

[08:47] James: any blockers we should be aware of?

[08:50] Laura: nothing on our side beyond network approvals and a slot for the sizing call. performance-wise we recommend doing a small load test with warm cache to validate p99 improvements.

[09:02] Samir: great. let's recap next steps — samir sends pricing and SOW, laura attaches benchmarks and CLI snippets, ravi provides usage export, maya prepares final QBR deck and adoption items, and we'll schedule the sizing call for first week of june.

[09:18] Elena: sounds good, appreciate it.

[09:22] James: thanks everyone.

[09:25] Samir: thanks team — talk soon.

End of transcript.
